title: [Epic] hole-loop experimental edition — concentric development
body:
## Intended experience / problem
The same words acquire another meaning because something has happened between encounters.

## Concrete deliverable
An isolated playable six-encounter edition, four working studies, recorded verification, creative evaluation, and an evidence-gated plan for expanded work.

## Dependencies
None. Independent of historical restoration PR #1.

## Scope
New experimental edition only, in experimental/six-encounters. Read-only source input; no restoration dependency or production route change. One repository until independent ownership, reuse or deployment is demonstrated.

## Acceptance criteria
- Circles 1 and 2 implemented and verified.
- Circles 3 and 4 have linked, explicit planned deliverables and evidence gates.
- Feature branch and reviewable PR.
- Planned / implemented / verified / artist-reviewed / deployed states remain distinct.

## Expected verification evidence
Experimental README; source census; engine/browser test reports; screenshots; evaluation; linked PR. No hosted preview is claimed without successful deployment.

## Priority and completion status
Assignment scope: Circles 1–2 implemented and verified; Circles 3–4 planned. Artist-reviewed: no. Deployed: no. Implemented and locally verified on the feature branch; merge is a separate state.

title: [Epic · Circle 1] Playable three-chamber core

title: [Circle 1] Eligible-display clock and lifecycle controls
body:
## Intended experience / problem
Timed departure must exclude hidden and paused intervals and preserve reader entry control.

## Concrete deliverable
Monotonic 5000ms clock, ready/visibility/pause wiring, cancellation and explicit mode choice/restart.

## Dependencies
sequence

## Scope
No timer at entrance; no attention measurement; manual and timer returns compete safely.

## Acceptance criteria
- 3000 + extended hidden + 1999 stays active.
- Eligible 5000ms tick returns once.
- Resume/visibility event alone never navigates.
- Reader-paced holds indefinitely.
- Exit/restart cancel pending progress.

## Expected verification evidence
Injected-clock boundary tests plus clock-controlled real-browser lifecycle checks and visibility-event simulation.

## Priority and completion status
Circle 1. Status: verified. Artist-reviewed: no. Deployed: no. Implemented and locally verified on the feature branch; merge is a separate state.

title: [Circle 3] Develop nine remaining chambers from their source language
body:
## Intended experience / problem
Dialogue, refusal, interruption, confinement and release should have distinct linguistic grounds.

## Concrete deliverable
Nine bounded prototypes with source-specific questions and behavior proposals listed below.

## Dependencies
evaluation, voice

## Scope
Read-only source text nodes at revision 9fc3c006f2764e1887b79293e32eb9a3a1875344; no historical asset recovery. All paths use provenance/original-2017/labyrinth/<ID>.html.txt.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each prototype preserves a baseline and names the changed rule.
- Source wording/order and attribution reviewed before adoption.
- Stop/exit/read access and return semantics remain clear.
- Do not add these to the score without evaluation.

## Expected verification evidence
Source census identities, prototype configs/captures and reader/artist decisions.

## Priority and completion status
Circle 3. Status: planned. Artist-reviewed: no. Deployed: no. No implementation is claimed for this planned scope.

## Source-specific proposals (planned)

| ID / source material | Proposed behavior | Question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 040615 · long passage beginning “I have tried to permanently subvert senses”, recurring failure clauses and isolated “o f” nodes | Confinement: expose a scrollable fixed-width passage, then offer an expanded reading plane with the same language | Does spatial restriction perform the effort/failure described, or merely obstruct reading? |
| 040715 · Poor Minotaur / where are you now / lost frown | Address: vary the distance between the invocation and successive questions | Does interval make the addressed figure seem absent, approaching or unreachable? |
| 040815 · “why did you lie / to me ?” and “because i am a wild / animal.” | Dialogue: reader reveals the reply separately, preserving clause order | Does withholding the reply change the apparent relationship between speakers? |
| 041315 · your / favors / do not / threaten / us | Refusal: stable word sequence with a comparison of weight concentrated on “your” versus “us” | Which speaker or addressee appears to control the refusal? |
| 041415 · can you pray for me, stephen / chainlink smile / complete sable / hamlet iago | Appeal/interruption: layers reveal these nodes in source order while a reading view remains complete | Does the appeal remain a frame for the fragments, or become one fragment among them? |
| 041715 · seven inspected lines beginning “April is the cruellest month” | Seasonal interval: compare continuous lines with controlled whitespace between the spring/winter sections | Does spatial interval alter the relation between memory, desire and shelter? |
| 042215 · spaced Sunday distraction / brood posession pulse / eyes without a face / beheading / final question | Interruption: successive reader-triggered frames retain a visible source-order map | Does interruption make distraction operate as a score, or destroy the phrase relationships? |
| 051815 · f a t e d / f a i t h f u l / f a t a l | Release: compare three parallel fields with a converging common reading plane | Do shared letter structures create relation without collapsing distinct words? |
| 072716 · two lines about proper sedation and a telephone number | Instruction/refusal: keep the source visible but require an explicit decision to return; no dial action | Does an inert instruction still appear authoritative? |

These are proposals, not implemented functions or documented original influences. Exact text nodes, including spelling/spacing, are in the census. Third-party quotation attribution and the status of the telephone text require artist/source review before any expanded public edition.
